GENERAL THEOREMS.
If $\sigma_{a}$ and $\sigma_{b}$ are the surface-densities and $\Psi_{a}$ and $\Psi_{b}$ the poten-
tials of the surfaces $a$ and $b$ respectively,
$$\begin{aligned}
& \sigma_{a}=\frac{1}{4 \pi}\left(\Psi_{a}-\Psi_{b}\right)\left[\frac{1}{b-a}+\frac{1}{8} \nabla^{2} a+\frac{1}{8} \nabla^{2} b\right] \\
& \sigma_{b}=\frac{1}{4 \pi}\left(\Psi_{b}-\Psi_{a}\right)\left[\frac{1}{b-a}-\frac{1}{6} \nabla^{2} a-\frac{1}{8} \nabla^{2} b\right] *
\end{aligned}$$
* \{This investigation is not very rigorous, and the expressions for the surface density
do not agree with the results obtained by rigorous methods for the cases of two
spheres, two cylinders, a sphere and plane, or a cylinder and plane placed close
together. We can obtain an expression for the surface density as follows. Let us
assume that the axis of $z$ is an axis of symmetry, then the axis will cut all the equi-
potential surfaces at right angles, and if $V$ is the potential, $R_{1} R_{2}$ the principal radii
of curvature of an equipotential surface where it is cut by the axis of $x$, the solenoidal
condition along the axis of $z$ may easily be shown to be
$$\frac{d^{2} V}{d z^{2}}+\left(\frac{1}{R_{1}}+\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right) \frac{d V}{d z}=0$$
If $V_{A}, V_{B}$ are the potentials of the two surfaces respectively, $t$ the distance between
the surfaces along the axis of $z$,
$$V_{B}=V_{A}+t\left(\frac{d V}{d z}\right)_{A}+1 t^{2}\left(\frac{d^{2} V}{d z^{2}}\right)_{A}+\ldots$$
or if $R_{A_{1}}, R_{A_{2}}$ denote the principal radii of curvature of the first surfaces, substituting
for $\frac{d^{2} V}{d z^{2}}$ from the differential equation, we get
but
$$\begin{gathered}
V_{B}-V_{A}=t\left(\frac{d V}{d z}\right)_{A}\left\{1-\frac{1}{2} t\left\{\frac{1}{R_{A_{1}}}+\frac{1}{R_{A_{2}}}\right\}\right\}+\ldots ; \\
\left(\frac{d V}{d z}\right)_{A}=-4 \pi \sigma_{A}
\end{gathered}$$
when $\sigma_{A}$ is the surface density where the axis of $z$ cut the first surface, hence
similarly
$$\begin{aligned}
& \sigma_{A}=\frac{1}{4 \pi} \frac{\left(V_{A}-V_{B}\right)}{t}\left\{1+\frac{1}{2} t\left\{\frac{1}{R_{A_{1}}}+\frac{1}{R_{A_{2}}}\right\}\right\} \text { approximately, } \\
& \sigma_{B}=\frac{1}{4 \pi} \frac{\left(V_{B}-V_{A}\right)}{t}\left\{1+\frac{1}{2} t\left\{\frac{1}{R_{B_{1}}}+\frac{1}{R_{B_{2}}}\right\}\right\} \text { approximately, }
\end{aligned}$$
and these expressions agree in the cases before mentioned with those obtained by
rigorous methods. \}
